summary: Officers were sent to a Walmart parking lot at 7:25 p.m. for a man reported to be loitering in the lot.
Officers were sent to a grocery store on Union Avenue at 7:35 p.m. where six people were reported to be fighting with security, one of them in a ski mask.

A traffic stop at Fremont Street and 9th Avenue at 7:58 p.m. turned into a foot chase. Two people ran from the car and a third was reported to possibly have a rifle; officers broadcast a code 33 and searched the area.
A crew was sent to a field reported on fire in a store parking lot off Tucker Road at 8:43 p.m.

Crews were sent to a house on South Silver Ridge Street at 8:53 p.m. for smoke and flames from an attached garage. Heavy smoke was showing from one side when they arrived, and no injuries were reported.
Officers were sent at 9:19 p.m. to a home where a woman was reported to be suicidal with a knife to her neck and her husband was telling her not to call 911.
Officers were sent to the 3500 block of Gilmore Avenue at 9:26 p.m. for a man reported to have walked into a yard.
A crew found a small utility truck on fire in the 10100 block of Main Street at 9:36 p.m. and handled it; the other engines were canceled.
Officers were sent to the 4300 block of Staples Court at 10:07 p.m. after a caller said a couple had become physical on the porch and were threatening the caller's mother.
Officers were sent to the Camilla Village apartments at 10:25 p.m. after a caller reported people pointing a firearm out of a vehicle window. The caller disconnected and did not answer a callback.
Officers were sent to Valley Plaza and Castro Lane at 10:36 p.m. for a group of juveniles reported to have firearms and knives and to be surrounding the caller.
Crews were sent at 10:45 p.m. to a bonfire in a field. The caller put it at under five feet across and no threat was reported.
Officers were sent to the 3400 block of Chester Avenue at 10:49 p.m. for a man reported to be asking people to call 911 without saying why.
A vehicle hit a pedestrian at 30th Street and Union Avenue at 11:33 p.m. Officers and medics responded, and the injuries were described as minor to moderate.

Officers were sent to an apartment complex on Terrace Way at 11:33 p.m. after callers reported 8 to 10 people in ski masks, some of them with firearms, banging on doors. Officers swept the complex and found no one.
Officers were sent to a party on Alder Glen Street at 11:35 p.m. for underage drinking, and a second caller then reported people with firearms at the party.

Officers were sent to Mohawk Street at 11:49 p.m. for shots fired and a chase. Two more people were detained, and officers said no one else was outstanding; a search of the field and a house south of it continued.
Officers were sent to a home just before midnight after a woman was heard yelling and then told a neighbor a man was trying to kill her.
A crew was sent to a vegetation fire off Copas Road at 12:01 a.m. The fire was reported out a few minutes later.

Deputies searched a backyard, a shed and an overhang at a home on Hageman Road at Ledgeview Lane from 12:05 to 1:07 a.m. for a man wanted on a served criminal protective order and reported to be hiding there. An air unit watched the yard, and the search was cleared at 1:07 a.m.
Deputies were sent to the 1800 block of East Brundage Lane at 12:24 a.m. for a possible drunk driver asleep at the wheel.

A traffic stop at South Fairfax Road and Oasis turned into a foot chase at 12:41 a.m. when the driver ran into a covered patio at a house on Garden Street. Deputies set a perimeter and reported two juveniles with him.

Deputies were sent to a gas station on Weedpatch Highway at 12:53 a.m. for a possible stabbing. A woman told a clerk her boyfriend had pulled a knife on her and she had blood on her hands, which she said could have come from a red bottle she was carrying.
An engine was sent to the Fairground RV Park on South Richmond Street at 1:26 a.m. for difficulty breathing.
Crews were sent to the 3200 block of Bucknell Street at 1:32 a.m. for a crash reported as two vehicles and found a single vehicle on its roof.

disposition: person still in the turn lane
summary: Officers were sent to Chester Avenue and California at 1:37 a.m. for a man lying in the turn lane who appeared to want to be hit by a vehicle. He was still there at 2:19 a.m., with bystanders trying to wake him and one offering CPR.
A car rolled at Stine Road and Berkshire Road at 1:58 a.m. and the driver was pinned in. The airbags had gone off, and the first report of a vehicle on fire was wrong.

Officers were sent to the 1000 block of Oregon Street at 2:13 a.m. for a domestic call. A physical struggle was heard on an open line before a man took the phone, said everything was fine and hung up.

A two-vehicle crash at White Lane and Cernan Court at 2:45 a.m. shut White Lane down in both directions, and one person was reported to be getting CPR at the scene. Crews blocked White Lane at Lily while they worked.
A vehicle struck a wooden light pole at 3:02 a.m. PG&E sent a crew to replace it, and CHP was not requested.
Deputies were sent at 3:13 a.m. to a home on Planz Road for a domestic violence call.

Deputies were called at 3:37 a.m. after a caller reported five shots and screaming. They found a victim, and subjects were reported fleeing in vehicles; one who ran on foot crossed to an apartment complex across the street. A caller reported blood in an alleyway. By 4:53 a.m. dispatch was working it as a homicide on South Half Moon Drive, with a briefing staged at Savory Lane and South Half Moon.
A crew sent to the 1200 block of University Avenue at 4:09 a.m. found a fire in a living room that was already out. Smoke was still inside the home.

Officers were sent to the 1600 block of Quincy Street at 4:12 a.m., where a neighbor was reported to have a firearm and to have pointed a laser at the caller. A disturbance was still going on when officers arrived.
A crew was sent to the 2100 block of San Luis Street at 4:23 a.m. for a traumatic injury.
Officers were sent to the 12600 block of Jasmine Avenue at 4:37 a.m. for a party where juveniles were reported to be drinking and driving recklessly.
Crews were sent at 4:46 a.m. to a grass fire in a field behind a new housing development. It was not close to the structures.
A crew was sent to a vegetation fire on Rosedale Highway at 5:11 a.m.
Officers were sent to the 4500 block of Mesa Drive at 5:23 a.m. on a report that a woman there was talking about suicide and wanting to cut herself, with two juveniles also at the home.
An officer moved to stop a white Acura reported to be swerving and holding up traffic on Stockdale Highway at 5:40 a.m.

disposition: man still reported armed with nails
summary: Officers were sent to the 3500 block of Country Club Drive at 5:43 a.m. where a man was reported to have stabbed his brother in the face with a nail and to still be trying to stab people. He had several nails with him.
Officers were sent to the alley of the 6700 block of Wilson Road at 5:43 a.m. for a woman reported to be hitting a garage with a flashlight.
Crews were sent at 5:56 a.m. to a vacant commercial warehouse where light and smoke were showing. They staged on arrival to investigate.
Road-rage collision and hit-and-run on Kirkcaldy Drive.
Commercial fire alarm at Panda Express.
Teen found unresponsive after pill and alcohol use.
Fire response at Southern Public Service Station.
Welfare check on person at Castle Lane apartment.
Suspicious person reported on Elsinore Street.
Possible shooting reported on Eureka Street.
